new_scholarship.description: The Government of the Republic of Ghana awards scholarships for full-time, on-campus undergraduate and postgraduate study at public tertiary education institutions in Ghana to qualified nationals of ECOWAS member states other than Ghana for the 2026/2027 academic year. Awards are made in priority fields aligned with regional development priorities, including medicine, nursing, public health, biomedical sciences, engineering, computer science, artificial intelligence, data science, cybersecurity, renewable energy, agribusiness, crop science, animal science, food technology, law and climate studies. Applications run through each applicant's home-country nominating agency, which is subject to a quota of three nominees per ECOWAS member state, so applicants cannot apply directly.

new_scholarship.description: The Ministry of Education of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia operates the Study in Saudi platform, which administers government scholarships for international students at Saudi universities. The platform's Study Visa & Pathways page sets out three funding tiers: Full Scholarships, described as 'Tuition, housing & living - all covered'; Partial Scholarships, described as covering part of tuition costs; and paid self-funded study programmes. Applications are made through the educational institution where the student intends to study, and the institution reviews the application and issues an admission decision before the Ministry of Education completes final admission procedures. The Ministry of Education publishes an application window for international and resident students for each semester, and the window for the Second Semester Academic Calendar 2026 ran from 16 September to 6 October 2026.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: The Study Visa & Pathways page states the common visa eligibility conditions: applicant aged 16 or over; a valid passport with at least six months' validity from the intended date of entry; acceptance from a licensed and accredited educational institution in the Kingdom; and written guardian consent for applicants under 18. Scholarship admission itself runs through the chosen institution's admissions process.

new_scholarship.english_requirement: Proof of proficiency in the language of study is required for the long-term study visa, except for applicants wishing to study Arabic. The platform does not publish a specific English test or score threshold.
new_scholarship.selection_notes: The platform publishes no selection criteria or weighting. Applications are assessed by the chosen educational institution, which 'will review your application and issue an admission decision accordingly'; after institutional approval, the Ministry of Education completes final admission procedures. An application status of 'Under Process' means the application is under review by the relevant institution.
new_scholarship.best_fit: International students aged 16 or over seeking a government-funded place at a participating Saudi university, particularly those needing full tuition, housing and living support, who can meet the institution's own admissions requirements and a 6 October 2026 platform deadline.
new_scholarship.notes: Admission and funding are not fully separated in the published process: the platform states 'You can apply for a scholarship through the educational institution where you wish to study by submitting an admission application', so funding is institution-mediated rather than applied for through a separate central scholarship form. Study in Saudi also runs Partial Scholarships and self-funded options, so the 'Fully Funded' label applies specifically to the Full Scholarships tier, which the Ministry of Education describes as covering tuition, housing and living. Applicants should note that application data other than contact information cannot be modified after submission. Separately, the Government of Ghana's Ghana Scholarships Authority published a complementary national notice (deadline 28 October 2026) channelling Ghanaian citizens to six named Saudi universities through this same platform.

programme_detail_official.description: Study in Saudi is the Ministry of Education's official platform for international students, researchers and professional learners, covering study, research and training at Saudi universities together with the educational visa pathway. Its Study Visa & Pathways page defines three funding routes: Full Scholarships, which the Ministry of Education describes as 'Tuition, housing & living - all covered'; Partial Scholarships, covering part of tuition costs; and paid self-funded study programmes. Students apply by submitting an admission application to the institution they wish to attend; the institution reviews it and issues an admission decision, and the Ministry of Education then completes final admission procedures. The Ministry publishes an application window for international and resident students each semester, and the currently published window for the Second Semester Academic Calendar 2026 closes on 6 October 2026.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia - more than 50 public and private universities listed on the platform

application_readiness_checklist: Complete your Study in Saudi platform profile first - the platform blocks programme applications while the profile is incomplete
Pick a participating institution from the platform's directory of more than 50 public and private universities, then a specific programme
Check that institution's own admissions requirements and deadlines, because they can be stricter and earlier than the platform's 6 October 2026 window
Confirm you meet the age floor of 16 and hold a passport valid at least six months beyond your intended entry date
Prepare proof of proficiency in the language of study unless you are studying Arabic
If staying over one year, arrange the medical report confirming freedom from infectious diseases and medical insurance for yourself and dependants
Get written guardian consent if you are under 18
Submit the admission application to the institution - this is also your scholarship application
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 6 October 2026 platform window, or the earlier institutional deadline that sits inside it
Applying while the platform profile is incomplete, which prevents programme applications entirely
Assuming the scholarship is applied for centrally - it is institution-mediated, so no application is lodged without an institutional admission decision
Applying to a programme in a language for which you cannot supply proof of proficiency, and not qualifying for the Arabic exemption
Failing the participating institution's own academic or language entry requirements, which are separate from the platform's visa conditions
Missing the medical report or medical insurance documentation for a long-term stay
Losing the ability to correct application data: only contact information can be changed after submission
Assuming the Full Scholarships tier applies automatically - the platform also offers Partial Scholarships and self-funded places, so the tier awarded is institution-dependent
estimated_uncovered_costs: Air fares to Saudi Arabia are not mentioned anywhere in the published material, so travel cost cannot be assumed covered
The Full Scholarships tier is stated as tuition, housing and living only, so any other charge the institution levies is not addressed
Costs arising between a student leaving home and the visa start date fall outside the award's stated components
No stipend amount, currency or payment schedule is published, so the cash value of the living component cannot be calculated from official sources
document_audit: Valid passport with at least 6 months validity from the intended date of entry - check the expiry date against your entry date, not today's date
Acceptance/confirmation from a licensed and accredited Saudi institution
Proof of proficiency in the language of study, or evidence that you are studying Arabic to claim the exemption
Medical report confirming freedom from infectious diseases (stays exceeding one year)
Medical insurance document covering the visa holder and any dependants
Guardian consent letter plus companion details if under 18
Verify every document is uploaded to the platform before submitting, since post-submission amendment is limited to contact information

new_scholarship.description: OIC-COMSTECH and member institutions of its Consortium of Excellence jointly offer short- to medium-term research placements for young researchers from OIC member states in agriculture, food security and related fields. The fellowship covers eight thematic areas: plant biotechnology; human nutrition; the water-food-energy nexus; food science and technology; nutraceuticals and the food-medicine continuum; agro-business, trade and food value chains; agricultural technology and innovations; and neglected food crops. Only 10 fellowships are available and they are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis subject to eligibility, so the call functions as a rolling award rather than a fixed-deadline competition. COMSTECH covers low-cost international airfare and visa fees where applicable, and host institutions are expected to provide accommodation, subsistence, supervision and mentoring.

Experience requirements differ by degree level, and applicants must be fluent in English and available full-time for the whole fellowship.

The stated rationale is that food insecurity remains a pressing global issue in many OIC countries, where economic instability, climate change, conflict and malnutrition have disrupted food systems, and that addressing this requires investment in research, knowledge transfer and capacity building. Ten fellowships are available per round and are awarded first-come, first-served. COMSTECH covers low-cost international airfare and visa fees where applicable, while host institutions provide accommodation, subsistence, supervision and mentoring.

new_scholarship.description: COMSTECH, together with key centres of excellence in OIC countries, runs a training scholarship in virology and vaccine technology for young scientists from OIC member states. Selected fellows spend three months at a relevant centre of excellence in another OIC country, and the aim is to strengthen research and development capacity among scientists early in their careers and to build linkages for further collaboration. Training themes include the epidemiology of viral diseases, biorisk assessment and the identification of zoonotic sources, development of diagnostics and therapeutics against viral outbreaks, real-time data collection on the spread of viral infections and preparation for future outbreaks, and vaccine development. COMSTECH provides international low-cost airfare, and host institutions are expected to provide subsistence, supervision and mentoring.

programme_detail_official.description: COMSTECH, with key centres of excellence in OIC countries, offers fellowships in research and advanced training in virology and vaccine technology to young scientists from OIC member states. Each fellow spends three months at a relevant centre of excellence in an OIC country other than their own. The stated rationale is that the devastation of the COVID-19 pandemic exposed weak preparedness and resilience in many countries of the South, with many OIC countries heavily dependent on others for diagnostic equipment, kits, ventilators and personal protective equipment, so that good science and robust public policy measures are required. Objectives include the epidemiology of viral diseases, biorisk assessment and zoonotic disease prevention, development of diagnostics and therapeutics against viral outbreaks, real-time data collection on viral spread and outbreak preparedness, and vaccine development.

programme_detail_official.description: COMSTECH and member institutions of its Consortium of Excellence jointly offer research fellowships to young women researchers, scientists and engineers in OIC countries to spend six to twelve months at a relevant centre of excellence in an OIC member state. The purpose is to enhance the research and development capacity of promising women researchers and engineers from OIC least-developed countries who are at the beginning of their research career, and to help them build linkages for further collaboration. The field is natural sciences, applied sciences, engineering and technology. The awarding body states that applications and nominations are open all around the year and records the call as currently open. COMSTECH bears international low-cost airfare, and host institutions are expected to provide accommodation, subsistence, supervision and mentoring.

new_scholarship.description: The EAC Scholarship Programme is a regional initiative of the East African Community and the Federal Republic of Germany, implemented by the Inter-University Council for East Africa. It funds academically talented but financially disadvantaged students from the eight EAC Partner States to pursue two-year Master's degrees at a participating university in a different EAC Partner State. Awards are restricted to six thematic areas - mathematics, engineering, informatics, science, technology and business science - and Cohort 4 offered up to 120 scholarships across 60 approved Master's programmes at partner universities in Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda and Tanzania. The scholarship package covers a return economy air ticket, full tuition paid directly to the host university, a EUR 200 arrival allowance, a monthly stipend of EUR 380, a EUR 650 lump sum for study materials, a one-time EUR 1,500 study and research allowance, medical insurance, and entry visa or student pass fees where required.

new_scholarship.description: The Petroleum Technology Development Fund is a Nigerian federal government agency mandated with developing indigenous human capacity and petroleum technology for the oil and gas industry. The Fund invites applications from qualified Nigerians for its 2026/27 Undergraduate, Master's and PhD scholarships, restricted to Nigerian public universities and to a published list of sponsored courses grouped into engineering, science, environmental science, renewable energy and management. Undergraduate applicants must already be at 200 level in a Nigerian public university and must hold a valid admission letter; MSc and PhD applicants must hold full-time admission letters and a minimum Second Class Lower (2:2) in an oil and gas-related field. Selection is merit-driven and explicitly weighted toward equitable representation of the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

A National Identity Number is mandatory before applying, and all applicants must submit a certificate of indigeneship.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: The scholarship is described as highly competitive and merit-driven. Undergraduate final selection is based on grades on transcripts, which must be signed and stamped by the HOD, Exams Officer or other authorised university personnel. Selection is based on equitable representation of the 36 states of the Federation and the Federal Capital Territory, except where a state does not have the requisite number of candidates to fill its allotted slots.
